tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).

1	# Marketing Plan: Handmade Candle Shop on Etsy
2	
3	**Written Nov 13, 2026 · Goal: $2,000 in November, $2,000 in December, then steady $3,000/month by April 2027 · Budget: $150/month · Time: 5 hours/week of marketing**
4	
5	> **Read this first.** You chose not to share your Etsy data, so every number about your shop below is an **estimate built from what you told me** (about 25 soy-jar listings at $18–32, 35–40 orders and about $1,200 a month, mostly from Etsy search, no ads yet). Every estimate is listed in the register at the end. Replace them with real stats in Week 1. The plan is built to be re-aimed once you do.
6	>
7	> **Assumption to check:** the 5 hours a week covers marketing only. Making candles, packing and shipping are on top of that. If your 5 hours must cover everything, tell me and I'll cut the plan down.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 1. The arithmetic behind the goal
12	
13	Revenue = visits × conversion rate × average order value. Every tactic in this plan moves one of those three.
14	
15	| Scenario | Visits/month | Conversion | Orders | Avg order | Revenue |
16	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
17	| Baseline (your estimate) | 1,850 | 2.0% | 37 | $32.4 | $1,199 |
18	| Holiday (December target) | 2,300 | 2.4% | 55 | $36.4 | $2,002 |
19	| Spring A (the plan) | 3,000 | 2.5% | 75 | $40.0 | $3,000 |
20	| Spring B (traffic only) | 4,100 | 2.2% | 90 | $33.3 | $2,997 |
21	
22	- **Spring A needs +62% traffic, a small conversion gain, and a $40 average order.** That is reachable with 5 hours and $150, because bundles and a free-shipping threshold do much of the work.
23	- **Spring B needs +122% traffic with no change in order value.** That is not reachable on this budget, so the plan does not follow it.
24	- The $40 average order is the lever you control most. Gift sets and add-ons get you there faster than any amount of social posting.
25	- **Visits and conversion (1,850 and 2.0%) are my guesses, not your data.** Week 1 replaces them with real figures.
26	
27	Weekly pace the scorecard will track:
28	
29	| Period | Visits/month | Orders/month | Revenue/month | Visits/week | Orders/week | Revenue/week |
30	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
31	| Baseline | 1,850 | 37 | $1,199 | 426 | 9 | $276 |
32	| Holiday (Dec) | 2,300 | 55 | $2,002 | 529 | 13 | $461 |
33	| Spring | 3,000 | 75 | $3,000 | 690 | 17 | $690 |
34	
35	**December's sales window is shorter than the month.** With USPS's Ground Advantage ship-by date at Dec 17, most gift revenue has to land between Black Friday and about Dec 14. That is roughly two and a half weeks, so Weeks 2–5 decide whether December reaches $2,000. Orders after Dec 17 are mostly late shoppers and post-Christmas buyers.
36	
37	**Is November's $2,000 realistic?** It's the hardest of your targets. If you're at about $1,200 on a normal pace, you'd have roughly $500–700 by Nov 13. That leaves about $1,300–1,500 for the last 17 days, roughly double your normal rate. Treat $2,000 as the stretch and about $1,600 as the floor. December, with the gift window open until the shipping cutoffs, is where $2,000 is most plausible. Enter your real month-to-date in Week 1 and the target gap becomes exact.
38	
39	## 2. Week 1 diagnosis: find your bottleneck
40	
41	Pull your last 30 days from Etsy Stats and check conversion (orders ÷ visits). The result decides where the next hours go.
42	
43	| If your conversion is | The bottleneck is | Do this first |
44	|---|---|---|
45	| Under 1.5% | The listings (photos, price, titles) | Fix the top 3 listings before spending on ads. Hold ad money until Week 3. |
46	| 1.5–3% | Traffic and order value | Follow the plan as written. |
47	| Over 3% | Traffic | Move extra budget into ads, and test a $2 price rise on your best seller. |
48	
49	Also check **traffic sources**. If more than about 80% comes from Etsy search, SEO and ads are your main levers, and social posting is a supporting act.
50	
51	## 3. How to read your numbers
52	
53	Your "uneven sales" may be partly just chance. At 37 orders a month, ordinary random variation alone gives a 95% range of **about 25 to 49 orders** (a standard deviation of about 6). A month of 28 followed by one of 46 can happen with nothing changing. Weekly orders swing even more: at about 9 a week, anything from 3 to 14 is normal.
54	
55	That has three consequences for how you judge tactics:
56	
57	1. **Judge on high-count numbers first.** Visits (about 1,850 a month, with a spread of only about 2%) and ad clicks are far more reliable than orders.
58	2. **Don't judge a tactic on one month of orders.** A genuine 25% lift in orders is only about 1 standard deviation above noise after one month, and reaches about 2 after four months.
59	3. **Conversion changes can't be proven at your size.** Telling 2.0% from 2.4% needs about 21,000 visits per version. Instead, judge listing changes by whether views and clicks rise over 8 or more weeks, and by what buyers say in reviews and messages.
60	
61	(These figures are computed in `check_plan.py`. They assume orders arrive at random; real shops are lumpier, so the true spread is at least this large.)
62	
63	## 4. Where the hours go
64	
65	Ranked by expected payoff per hour, for a shop of your size:
66	
67	| # | Lever | What it moves | Hours/week (avg) |
68	|---|---|---|---|
69	| 1 | Rebuild listings: titles, tags, first photo, gift cues | Visits, conversion | 1.5–2 |
70	| 2 | Gift sets, add-ons and a free-shipping threshold | Order value | 1–1.5 |
71	| 3 | Etsy Ads on proven listings | Visits | 0.5 |
72	| 4 | Reviews and repeat buyers (inserts, email) | Conversion, repeat orders | 0.5–1 |
73	| 5 | One video pipeline: film once, post to Instagram Reels and Pinterest | Visits | 1–1.5 |
74	| 6 | Weekly scorecard and kill-or-keep | Decisions | 0.5 |
75	
76	**Parked until after April (don't do these now):** a separate TikTok strategy, wholesale or consignment, craft markets, press and gift-guide pitching, and your own website. Each is a real option, but none fits 5 hours and $150 while Etsy search is your engine.
77	
78	### The listing rebuild
79	
80	- **Title:** put the phrase a gift buyer would type first, then the scent and size. For example: `Lavender Soy Candle Gift for Her, Hand Poured 8oz Jar, Relaxing Spa Candle`. Use most of the 140 characters, but make it read naturally.
81	- **13 tags, all used:** roughly 4 gift or occasion (birthday gift for her, housewarming gift), 4 scent or mood, 3 material or handmade, 2 style or room.
82	- **Photos, in this order:** (1) clean first image that reads at thumbnail size, (2) lit candle in a styled room, (3) scale shot, (4) label and wick close-up, (5) burn time and ingredients graphic, (6) gift-ready packaging, (7–10) scent variants and packing. Add a 5–15 second video: pouring, lighting or unboxing.
83	- **Description:** keywords and the hook in the first 160 characters, then wax, wick, burn time, size and care.
84	- **Method:** top 3 listings in Week 1, then 5 a week in January until all 25 are done.
85	
86	### Order value and the shipping threshold
87	
88	- Etsy launched its free-shipping guarantee in 2019: shops that ship free on US orders of **$35 or more** get priority in US search ([Etsy investor release](https://investors.etsy.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/117/etsy-unveils-plans-to-make-free-shipping-a-core-part-of-the-shopping-experience)). I could not confirm that this is still how search works today, so **verify the current rule in Shop Manager and treat the guarantee as a decision, not a default.** Your average order of about $32 sits just under $35.
89	- **The catch is profit.** Free shipping turns postage from a cost the buyer pays into a cost you pay. The margin check below shows that a bundle built to cross the threshold can earn *less* per order than a plain jar.
90	- Price ladder: mini or sample $8–14, core jar $22–32, gift sets and multi-candle bundles $38–65. For reference, roundups report a $25 single soy candle and a $55 boxed set of four travel candles as customer favorites ([Apartment Therapy](https://www.apartmenttherapy.com/candles-on-etsy-36653171)). That is secondhand reporting, so treat it as a rough benchmark.
91	
92	### Margin check: does the order-value lever raise profit?
93	
94	Revenue targets say nothing about what you keep. Etsy fees are about 6.5% transaction plus 3% + $0.25 payment processing, plus a $0.20 listing fee per sale (secondary sources: [Checkout Page](https://checkoutpage.com/blog/etsy-fees)). I use 9.5% of the order plus $0.45. Offsite Ads, when an order is attributed to one, take a further 12–15% of the order.
95	
96	Illustrative figures, **all my estimates**: an 8 oz jar costs you $9 in materials, a mini $3.50, and postage runs $8–12 per package (inferred from published Ground Advantage prices; your Etsy label screen shows the real cost). Replace these with your own.
97	
98	| Case | Order | Etsy fees | Materials | Postage you pay | Profit | Profit if Offsite Ad |
99	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
100	| A. 1 jar $28 + $7 shipping paid by buyer | $35 | $3.78 | $9.00 | $9.00 | $13.23 | $7.98 |
101	| B. Jar + mini add-on, $38, free shipping | $38 | $4.06 | $12.50 | $9.50 | $11.94 | $6.24 |
102	| C. 2-jar set, $52, free shipping | $52 | $5.39 | $18.00 | $12.00 | $16.61 | $8.81 |
103	| D. 3-mini set, $38, free shipping | $38 | $4.06 | $10.50 | $8.00 | $15.44 | $9.74 |
104	| E. 2-jar set, $38, free shipping | $38 | $4.06 | $18.00 | $12.00 | $3.94 | $-1.76 |
105	
106	What this shows:
107	- **A $38 two-jar set (E) is the trap.** It clears the threshold and earns about $4. A two-jar set needs a price of about **$47 or more** to reach $12 profit with free shipping.
108	- **Light sets (D) and add-on minis (B) are the better order-value levers.** They add revenue without adding much postage.
109	- **Offsite Ads cut profit per order by $5–$8 on attributed orders.** Case E goes negative.
110	- **Rule for every bundle you build: at least $12 profit per order** by your own materials and postage numbers. Check it before listing.
111	- At about $12–16 profit per order, 75 orders a month in spring is roughly **$900–$1,250 gross profit, before your $150 marketing spend.** The same maths at the baseline (37 orders at about $13) is about $490.
112	
113	
114	### Etsy Ads
115	
116	Etsy Ads uses **one daily budget for the whole shop**, with a $1 minimum ([Etsy Help](https://help.etsy.com/hc/articles/360033701174)). You choose which listings to promote and Etsy spreads the budget between them, so you can't set a separate amount per listing. Start by promoting your top 2 listings by conversion. In November–December the budget is $80 a month (about $2.65 a day). In January–April it is $60 (about $2 a day). Etsy's seller handbook suggests $3–5 a day for a first test, so ours is a lean test and its results will be noisy (Section 3).
117	
118	**Offsite Ads are separate from Etsy Ads, and may already apply to you.** Etsy charges 15% of an attributed order if your shop sold under $10,000 in the past 365 days (optional), or 12% if it sold $10,000 or more (mandatory). Etsy checks on the first day of each month, and once you cross $10,000 the 12% rate stays permanently ([Etsy Help](https://help.etsy.com/hc/en-in/articles/360000338367-How-Etsy-s-Offsite-Ads-Work), [Etsy fees](https://www.etsy.com/au/help/article/4530)). If you have averaged $1,200 a month for a year, you are probably already over $10,000. Check your Shop Manager and include the fee in your pricing.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

tools.name: WebSearch
tools.description:
Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

- The current month is (provided in the conversation below) — use this when searching for recent information.
- `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` filter results.
- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

mode.description: "standard": the normal web search: quick and cheap; right for straightforward lookups (reference facts, official pages, documentation, well-known people, places and topics) and simple follow-up lookups. "extended": a thorough, fresh search at several times the cost and latency.

Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

1	# Marketing Plan: Handmade Candle Shop on Etsy
2	
3	**Written Nov 13, 2026 · Goal: $2,000 in November, $2,000 in December, then steady $3,000/month by April 2027 · Budget: $150/month · Time: 5 hours/week of marketing**
4	
5	> **Read this first.** You chose not to share your Etsy data, so every number about your shop below is an **estimate built from what you told me** (about 25 soy-jar listings at $18–32, 35–40 orders and about $1,200 a month, mostly from Etsy search, no ads yet). Every estimate is listed in the register at the end. Replace them with real stats in Week 1. The plan is built to be re-aimed once you do.
6	>
7	> **Assumption to check:** the 5 hours a week covers marketing only. Making candles, packing and shipping are on top of that. If your 5 hours must cover everything, tell me and I'll cut the plan down.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 1. The arithmetic behind the goal
12	
13	Revenue = visits × conversion rate × average order value. Every tactic in this plan moves one of those three.
14	
15	| Scenario | Visits/month | Conversion | Orders | Avg order | Revenue |
16	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
17	| Baseline (your estimate) | 1,850 | 2.0% | 37 | $32.4 | $1,199 |
18	| Holiday (December target) | 2,300 | 2.4% | 55 | $36.4 | $2,002 |
19	| Spring A (the plan) | 3,000 | 2.5% | 75 | $40.0 | $3,000 |
20	| Spring B (traffic only) | 4,100 | 2.2% | 90 | $33.3 | $2,997 |
21	
22	- **Spring A needs +62% traffic, a small conversion gain, and a $40 average order.** That is reachable with 5 hours and $150, because bundles and a free-shipping threshold do much of the work.
23	- **Spring B needs +122% traffic with no change in order value.** That is not reachable on this budget, so the plan does not follow it.
24	- The $40 average order is the lever you control most. Gift sets and add-ons get you there faster than any amount of social posting.
25	- **Visits and conversion (1,850 and 2.0%) are my guesses, not your data.** Week 1 replaces them with real figures.
26	
27	Weekly pace the scorecard will track:
28	
29	| Period | Visits/month | Orders/month | Revenue/month | Visits/week | Orders/week | Revenue/week |
30	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
31	| Baseline | 1,850 | 37 | $1,199 | 426 | 9 | $276 |
32	| Holiday (Dec) | 2,300 | 55 | $2,002 | 529 | 13 | $461 |
33	| Spring | 3,000 | 75 | $3,000 | 690 | 17 | $690 |
34	
35	**December's sales window is shorter than the month.** With USPS's Ground Advantage ship-by date at Dec 17, most gift revenue has to land between Black Friday and about Dec 14. That is roughly two and a half weeks, so Weeks 2–5 decide whether December reaches $2,000. Orders after Dec 17 are mostly late shoppers and post-Christmas buyers.
36	
37	**Is November's $2,000 realistic?** It's the hardest of your targets. If you're at about $1,200 on a normal pace, you'd have roughly $500–700 by Nov 13. That leaves about $1,300–1,500 for the last 17 days, roughly double your normal rate. Treat $2,000 as the stretch and about $1,600 as the floor. December, with the gift window open until the shipping cutoffs, is where $2,000 is most plausible. Enter your real month-to-date in Week 1 and the target gap becomes exact.
38	
39	## 2. Week 1 diagnosis: find your bottleneck
40	
41	Pull your last 30 days from Etsy Stats and check conversion (orders ÷ visits). The result decides where the next hours go.
42	
43	| If your conversion is | The bottleneck is | Do this first |
44	|---|---|---|
45	| Under 1.5% | The listings (photos, price, titles) | Fix the top 3 listings before spending on ads. Hold ad money until Week 3. |
46	| 1.5–3% | Traffic and order value | Follow the plan as written. |
47	| Over 3% | Traffic | Move extra budget into ads, and test a $2 price rise on your best seller. |
48	
49	Also check **traffic sources**. If more than about 80% comes from Etsy search, SEO and ads are your main levers, and social posting is a supporting act.
50	
51	## 3. How to read your numbers
52	
53	Your "uneven sales" may be partly just chance. At 37 orders a month, ordinary random variation alone gives a 95% range of **about 25 to 49 orders** (a standard deviation of about 6). A month of 28 followed by one of 46 can happen with nothing changing. Weekly orders swing even more: at about 9 a week, anything from 3 to 14 is normal.
54	
55	That has three consequences for how you judge tactics:
56	
57	1. **Judge on high-count numbers first.** Visits (about 1,850 a month, with a spread of only about 2%) and ad clicks are far more reliable than orders.
58	2. **Don't judge a tactic on one month of orders.** A genuine 25% lift in orders is only about 1 standard deviation above noise after one month, and reaches about 2 after four months.
59	3. **Conversion changes can't be proven at your size.** Telling 2.0% from 2.4% needs about 21,000 visits per version. Instead, judge listing changes by whether views and clicks rise over 8 or more weeks, and by what buyers say in reviews and messages.
60	
61	(These figures are computed in `check_plan.py`. They assume orders arrive at random; real shops are lumpier, so the true spread is at least this large.)
62	
63	## 4. Where the hours go
64	
65	Ranked by expected payoff per hour, for a shop of your size:
66	
67	| # | Lever | What it moves | Hours/week (avg) |
68	|---|---|---|---|
69	| 1 | Rebuild listings: titles, tags, first photo, gift cues | Visits, conversion | 1.5–2 |
70	| 2 | Gift sets, add-ons and a free-shipping threshold | Order value | 1–1.5 |
71	| 3 | Etsy Ads on proven listings | Visits | 0.5 |
72	| 4 | Reviews and repeat buyers (inserts, email) | Conversion, repeat orders | 0.5–1 |
73	| 5 | One video pipeline: film once, post to Instagram Reels and Pinterest | Visits | 1–1.5 |
74	| 6 | Weekly scorecard and kill-or-keep | Decisions | 0.5 |
75	
76	**Parked until after April (don't do these now):** a separate TikTok strategy, wholesale or consignment, craft markets, press and gift-guide pitching, and your own website. Each is a real option, but none fits 5 hours and $150 while Etsy search is your engine.
77	
78	### The listing rebuild
79	
80	- **Title:** put the phrase a gift buyer would type first, then the scent and size. For example: `Lavender Soy Candle Gift for Her, Hand Poured 8oz Jar, Relaxing Spa Candle`. Use most of the 140 characters, but make it read naturally.
81	- **13 tags, all used:** roughly 4 gift or occasion (birthday gift for her, housewarming gift), 4 scent or mood, 3 material or handmade, 2 style or room.
82	- **Photos, in this order:** (1) clean first image that reads at thumbnail size, (2) lit candle in a styled room, (3) scale shot, (4) label and wick close-up, (5) burn time and ingredients graphic, (6) gift-ready packaging, (7–10) scent variants and packing. Add a 5–15 second video: pouring, lighting or unboxing.
83	- **Description:** keywords and the hook in the first 160 characters, then wax, wick, burn time, size and care.
84	- **Method:** top 3 listings in Week 1, then 5 a week in January until all 25 are done.
85	
86	### Order value and the shipping threshold
87	
88	- Etsy launched its free-shipping guarantee in 2019: shops that ship free on US orders of **$35 or more** get priority in US search ([Etsy investor release](https://investors.etsy.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/117/etsy-unveils-plans-to-make-free-shipping-a-core-part-of-the-shopping-experience)). I could not confirm that this is still how search works today, so **verify the current rule in Shop Manager and treat the guarantee as a decision, not a default.** Your average order of about $32 sits just under $35.
89	- **The catch is profit.** Free shipping turns postage from a cost the buyer pays into a cost you pay. The margin check below shows that a bundle built to cross the threshold can earn *less* per order than a plain jar.
90	- Price ladder: mini or sample $8–14, core jar $22–32, gift sets and multi-candle bundles $38–65. For reference, roundups report a $25 single soy candle and a $55 boxed set of four travel candles as customer favorites ([Apartment Therapy](https://www.apartmenttherapy.com/candles-on-etsy-36653171)). That is secondhand reporting, so treat it as a rough benchmark.
91	
92	### Margin check: does the order-value lever raise profit?
93	
94	Revenue targets say nothing about what you keep. Etsy fees are about 6.5% transaction plus 3% + $0.25 payment processing, plus a $0.20 listing fee per sale (secondary sources: [Checkout Page](https://checkoutpage.com/blog/etsy-fees)). I use 9.5% of the order plus $0.45. Offsite Ads, when an order is attributed to one, take a further 12–15% of the order.
95	
96	Illustrative figures, **all my estimates**: an 8 oz jar costs you $9 in materials, a mini $3.50, and postage runs $8–12 per package (inferred from published Ground Advantage prices; your Etsy label screen shows the real cost). Replace these with your own.
97	
98	| Case | Order | Etsy fees | Materials | Postage you pay | Profit | Profit if Offsite Ad |
99	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
100	| A. 1 jar $28 + $7 shipping paid by buyer | $35 | $3.78 | $9.00 | $9.00 | $13.23 | $7.98 |
101	| B. Jar + mini add-on, $38, free shipping | $38 | $4.06 | $12.50 | $9.50 | $11.94 | $6.24 |
102	| C. 2-jar set, $52, free shipping | $52 | $5.39 | $18.00 | $12.00 | $16.61 | $8.81 |
103	| D. 3-mini set, $38, free shipping | $38 | $4.06 | $10.50 | $8.00 | $15.44 | $9.74 |
104	| E. 2-jar set, $38, free shipping | $38 | $4.06 | $18.00 | $12.00 | $3.94 | $-1.76 |
105	
106	What this shows:
107	- **A $38 two-jar set (E) is the trap.** It clears the threshold and earns about $4. A two-jar set needs a price of about **$47 or more** to reach $12 profit with free shipping.
108	- **Light sets (D) and add-on minis (B) are the better order-value levers.** They add revenue without adding much postage.
109	- **Offsite Ads cut profit per order by $5–$8 on attributed orders.** Case E goes negative.
110	- **Rule for every bundle you build: at least $12 profit per order** by your own materials and postage numbers. Check it before listing.
111	- At about $12–16 profit per order, 75 orders a month in spring is roughly **$900–$1,250 gross profit, before your $150 marketing spend.** The same maths at the baseline (37 orders at about $13) is about $490.
112	
113	
114	### Etsy Ads
115	
116	Etsy Ads uses **one daily budget for the whole shop**, with a $1 minimum ([Etsy Help](https://help.etsy.com/hc/articles/360033701174)). You choose which listings to promote and Etsy spreads the budget between them, so you can't set a separate amount per listing. Start by promoting your top 2 listings by conversion. In November–December the budget is $80 a month (about $2.65 a day). In January–April it is $60 (about $2 a day). Etsy's seller handbook suggests $3–5 a day for a first test, so ours is a lean test and its results will be noisy (Section 3).
117	
118	**Offsite Ads are separate from Etsy Ads, and may already apply to you.** Etsy charges 15% of an attributed order if your shop sold under $10,000 in the past 365 days (optional), or 12% if it sold $10,000 or more (mandatory). Etsy checks on the first day of each month, and once you cross $10,000 the 12% rate stays permanently ([Etsy Help](https://help.etsy.com/hc/en-in/articles/360000338367-How-Etsy-s-Offsite-Ads-Work), [Etsy fees](https://www.etsy.com/au/help/article/4530)). If you have averaged $1,200 a month for a year, you are probably already over $10,000. Check your Shop Manager and include the fee in your pricing.

entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

- The current month is (provided in the conversation below) — use this when searching for recent information.

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

mode.description: "standard": the normal web search: quick and cheap; right for straightforward lookups (reference facts, official pages, documentation, well-known people, places and topics) and simple follow-up lookups. "extended": a thorough, fresh search at several times the cost and latency.

- **Free product counts.** The FTC's own influencer guide says a material connection includes a financial relationship such as a brand giving free or discounted products. A "material connection" to the brand includes a personal, family, or employment relationship or a financial relationship – such as the brand paying you or giving you free or discounted products or services.
- **Disclosure applies even when the gift is unrelated to the endorsed item.** Under the 2023 updates, "material connections" warranting disclosure can arise from many connections, including the nature of a relationship, free or discounted products (even where those products are unrelated to the endorsed product).

I found 10 problems in the plan. Three are legal or compliance gaps, three are money problems (the plan's own margin rule, the creator-gifting budget, and the December timing), and four are weak-method or planning gaps. They run from most to least severe. I checked each rule by web search and name the source. Search snippets and secondary guides were all I could reach, so for those rules I say what is verified and what is not.

**Checked and found correct:** The scenario, weekly-pace, fee and profit-table arithmetic reconciles. All 24 weekly task tables sum to 5.0 hours, and both budget columns sum to $150. The calendar dates are correct. USPS's Dec 17 (Ground Advantage) and Dec 18 (Priority) recommended ship-by dates are confirmed, and USPS says they are recommendations, not guarantees ([USPS](https://www.usps.com/holiday/holiday-shipping-dates.htm), [news3lv](https://news3lv.com/news/local/usps-announces-2026-holiday-shipping-deadlines-for-christmas-delivery)).

## Findings

**1. HIGH. Creator gifting has no FTC disclosure step, and it is underfunded.**
- Plan lines: "Creator gifting: pitch 10 micro-creators, send sample sets to 6", "Collect and repost creator content", and "At least 1 order or 3 usable photos per 6 samples sent".
- Verified: The FTC says free or discounted product is a "material connection" that must be disclosed. The brand must monitor what endorsers post, even for unsolicited free product ([FTC influencer guide](https://www.ftc.gov/system/files/ftc_gov/pdf/1001A_Influencer%20Guide_508.pdf), [ftc.gov/influencer](https://ftc.gov/influencer), [infolawgroup summary of the 2023 Endorsement Guides](https://infolawgroup.com/insights/2023/7/31/ftc-releases-updated-endorsement-guides-10-key-takeaways)).
- Why it matters: The plan never tells the owner to require disclosure or check posts. The owner is exposed, and so are the creators. The "usable photos per batch" test also rewards pressuring creators for content. Reposting needs written permission, and the plan doesn't say so. The creators' households also get lit candles with no safety guidance (see #2).
- Money: By the plan's own cost numbers (3-mini set at $10.50 materials plus $8 postage), 6 sets cost about $111. The creator budget line is $10 in Nov–Dec and $30 in Jan–Apr.
- Fix:
  - Include a one-line brief with each package: "#gifted / #sponsored, say so in the post".
  - Check each post and ask for a fix if it lacks the disclosure.
  - Get written permission before reposting.
  - Cut the batch to 2–3 sets, or raise the line item.
  - Drop the "photos per sample" quota.

**2. HIGH. The safety and labelling risk is a single vague line and has no budget.**
- Plan line: "Include warning labels, follow the candle labeling rules in your region, and consider product liability insurance."
- Verified (secondary sources only):
  - Lead-cored wicks are banned (16 CFR 1500.17).
  - ASTM F2058 fire-safety labelling is voluntary but treated as the industry standard.
  - Candles containing a hazardous substance under the FHSA need cautionary labelling.
  - Sources: [CPSC candle guidance](https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Business-Education/Business-Guidance/Candles), [CPSC voluntary standards](https://cpsc.gov/Regulations-Laws--Standards/Voluntary-Standards/Candles-and-Candle-Accessories), [Craftybase](https://craftybase.com/blog/legal-requirements-for-selling-homemade-candles).
- Not verified: Whether Prop 65 or state rules apply to the owner's fragrance oils.
- Why it matters: Fire and burn harm to buyers, kids and pets. The owner also faces uninsured product-liability exposure while volume rises about 50% in December and bundles and gifts to strangers are added. Insurance appears nowhere in the $150 budget. Copy like "Relaxing Spa Candle" and the burn-time graphic also need real support.
- Fix:
  - Add a Week 1 task: check labels against F2058 wording, confirm wicks are lead-free, and get fragrance-oil SDS and IFRA documents from the supplier.
  - Get an insurance quote before any gifting or the wedding-favor listing.
  - Add a budget line for it.
  - Test the burn time before publishing it.

**3. HIGH. The margin rule contradicts the plan's own table, and the offsite-ad rate is probably wrong.**
- Plan lines: "Rule for every bundle you build: at least $12 profit per order"; "Light sets (D) and add-on minis (B) are the better order-value levers"; and "10% off orders $40+".
- Case B earns $11.94, which fails the $12 rule. It also earns less than the plain jar (A, $13.23), so raising order value lowers profit per order.
- Case C (the only bundle that clears the $40 sale threshold) falls to about $11.90 once the 10% discount is applied. I computed this from the plan's own inputs. Every bundle at $38 is below the threshold.
- Verified: Etsy charges 12%, mandatory and permanent, once a shop has made $10,000 or more in any 365 days. It charges 15%, optional, below that ([Etsy Help](https://help.etsy.com/hc/articles/360000338367), [Etsy fees](https://www.etsy.com/help/article/4530)). At $1,200 a month (about $14,400 a year), the owner is probably already at the 12% mandatory tier. The table's "Profit if Offsite Ad" column uses 15%.
- Fix:
  - Price B at $39 or more, or drop it.
  - Rerun the table at 12%.
  - Test each bundle after the sale discount.
  - Make "check Offsite Ads status" a gate before building bundles.

**4. HIGH. The December target and timing contradict each other, and inventory is never planned.**
- The weekly-pace table spreads $2,002 evenly (about $461 a week), but the text says most revenue lands in a window of roughly 2.5 weeks, from Black Friday to Dec 14. That window needs about $800 a week, roughly double.
- The "last order Mon Dec 14 if you need 2–3 days to make and ship" assumes make-to-order. Soy candles usually need a cure period of days to weeks, though I have not verified this and it depends on the owner's wax. The restock check is in Week 5 (Dec 14) "for January", which is too late for the peak.
- Nothing sizes holiday stock. Materials for about 50% more volume are cash outside the $150, and there is leftover-inventory risk on seasonal sets.
- The "Last chance to order" posts on Dec 14 sit on the cutoff day itself.
- Fix:
  - In Week 1, set a production and stock plan (cure time, units per top-3 scent, cash cap).
  - Restate December pace for the real window.
  - Move the countdown to Dec 7–13.

**5. MEDIUM. The ad plan contradicts itself, and its decision rules can't fire.**
- Plan lines: Week 1 "Start Etsy Ads" (unconditional), versus Section 2 "Under 1.5%… Hold ad money until Week 3", and Week 4 "shift budget to the listing with more clicks per dollar".
- The plan itself says Etsy Ads has a single shop-wide budget with no per-listing amount, so shifting budget to one listing is impossible. The owner can only add or remove listings.
- The kill rules need 100 clicks (about $80, a full month's budget) and 5+ attributed orders. At about 2% conversion, that is not reached in Weeks 4–7 when the decisions are scheduled.
- Fix:
  - Gate the Week 1 ad start on the diagnosis.
  - Reword the Week 4 task as "remove the weaker listing".
  - Decide ads on clicks and cost per click through January, or pause the ads rather than judge them on noise.

**6. MEDIUM. The review-request and insert design carries Etsy policy risk.**
- Plan lines: "one plain message per order delivered…" (repeated about 6 times), plus a thank-you card and a separate "return-buyer code" card.
- Verified: Etsy's House Rules bar unsolicited promotion in Messages. A neutral review request is generally acceptable, but incentives tied to a star rating are not ([Etsy House Rules](https://www.etsy.com/help/article/4508), [Value Added Resource](https://www.valueaddedresource.net/etsy-cyber-special-message/)). This rests on secondary sources and I did not read the current Seller Policy text.
- Why it matters: Bundling a discount code with a review request in the same package invites an "incentivised review" reading. Messages to buyers about codes would be unsolicited promotion.
- Fix:
  - Keep the code only on the insert, and never mention it in Messages.
  - Rely on Etsy's own review reminders, and cap manual messages to one per order.
  - Keep the review wording identical to what the plan already says: no stars, no offer.

**7. MEDIUM. The email setup omits the CAN-SPAM basics.**
- Plan line: "Email only people who opt in; never import buyer addresses from Etsy."
- Verified (vendor sources, not the FTC page itself): Commercial email needs a valid physical postal address, a working unsubscribe, and opt-outs honoured within 10 business days. Penalties are per email ([sender.net](https://www.sender.net/blog/can-spam-compliance/), [transcend.io](https://transcend.io/blog/can-spam-act)). Confirm against the FTC's CAN-SPAM compliance guide.
- Why it matters: A one-person home-based shop must put an address in every email, and may not want to use the home address.
- Fix: In Week 8, add "choose the address (PO box or mailbox), turn on the footer and unsubscribe, and test the opt-out".

**8. MEDIUM. The tests are confounded, and some kill rules can never fail.**
- Plan lines: the Week 12 price test ("raise 3 best sellers by $2… 4 weeks"), the sale rule ("orders 25% or more higher than the previous period of the same length"), and "Orders hold within normal variation".
